The contrast between the sexes in body size likely drives differential foraging strategies and home-range requirements, with males predicted to have a higher absolute energy budget to support their larger frame.

The annual reproductive frequency, with just one litter per year, further limits the species’ capacity for rapid population growth and makes it particularly vulnerable to stochastic environmental perturbations or sustained reductions in adult female survival.
